questions.question: What is the number of bones in the vertebral column?

suspectLines.text: The vertebral column consists of 33 bones. The source lists 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 4 coccygeal vertebrae, while noting frequent variability and reported totals between 32 and 35.

questions.explanation:
The vertebral column consists of 33 bones. The source lists 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 4 coccygeal vertebrae, while noting frequent variability and reported totals between 32 and 35.

The vertebral column is about 70 cm long in males and about 60 cm in females on average and functions in support, protection of the spinal cord and nerves, muscle attachment and hematopoiesis.

questions.question: A 44-year-old man is brought to the casualty with a suspected whiplash injury following a road traffic accident. Which ligament would be injured in this condition?

suspectLines.text: Whiplash is a cervical acceleration-deceleration injury with hyperextension followed by recoil flexion. The anterior longitudinal ligament is a strong band along the anterior vertebral bodies, extending from the basilar occiput to upper sacrum and attaching at the anterior tubercle of C1 and body of C2.

questions.explanation:
The clinical scenario is suggestive of whiplash injury, in which the anterior longitudinal ligament of the spine is damaged.

Whiplash is a cervical acceleration-deceleration injury with hyperextension followed by recoil flexion. The anterior longitudinal ligament is a strong band along the anterior vertebral bodies, extending from the basilar occiput to upper sacrum and attaching at the anterior tubercle of C1 and body of C2.
